newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa sinks, March nears 920 stg support.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa sinks, March nears 920 stg support.

text.p: London cocoa futures sank in long liquidation on Friday facing a battle with support but traders were unable to cite any fundamental reasons behind the move.
The benchmark March position stood 10 stg down at 922 a tonne at midsession. Nearby support is cited at 920 stg. Other contracts lost up to 13 stg.
Traders said origins were absent in Friday's sales. Some scale-down buying by trade and possibly industry was also cited. Volume totalled 2,600 lots. The March/March switch was trading at 70-72 stg.
Traders noted an estimate by Robert Fish, managing director of UK-based research group PCR Ltd who said on Thursday that Ivory Coast's 1996/97 crop would be at least one million tonnes.
The projection came a day after an Ivorian diplomat estimated the total crop at 850,000 to 900,00 tonnes including the mid crop because the weather has not been kind this year.
"If the lower level is taken as a barometer of the likely yield in Ivory Coast, then we would be looking at a crop of around 960,000 tonnes for the year as a whole," broker GNI said.
Earlier, the head of Ghana's Cocoa Board John Henry Newman, forecast a total crop of between 320,000 to 340,000 tonnes.

In other news, the Ghana Cocoa Board said on Friday Ghana cocoa purchases in the sixth week of the 1996/97 season ending November 21 amounted to 18,519 tonnes compared with 28,686 tonnes in the same periof of the year-earlier season.

It said cumulative purchases at the end of the sixth week were 135,451 tonnes compared with 187,331 by November 23 last year which corresponded to the seventh week of the 1995/96 season. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8072
